newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B share indices end mixed after gains.
newsitem.headline: China's B share indices end mixed after gains.

text.p: China's B shares stock indices closed mixed in active trading on Thursday after sharp gains over the past few days, while the domestic A share markets fell, brokers said.

Shanghai's B shares fell on a correction in line with its A share counterpart, with the index down 0.94 percent to 70.944 points and turnover up to $18.1 million from Wednesday's $15.6 million, brokers said.

Shenzhen's B index ended sharply higher in heavy trading with institutions encouraged by the market's recent rises, brokers said. It rose 2.05 percent to close at 165.53 with turnover expanding to HK$269.6 million ($34.77 million) from HK$146.2 million.
"Domestic investors began profit-taking after the consecutive rises of the past few days," one Shanghai broker said. "But trading remained active on bargain-hunting."
But Shenzhen brokers said the day's rise was a follow-up to Wednesday's solid performance.

On the Shanghai B share market, textile machinery maker Shanghai Erfangji Co was the biggest loser on expectations of poor 1996 results despite active domestic speculative buying, slipping 7.21 percent to $0.18.
Real estate developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development traded the most on institutional buying, ending down 0.21 percent to $0.932.
On Shenzhen's B share market, television tube maker Shenzhen SEG Co was the biggest gainer and jumped 7.23 percent to HK$7.56.
Chiwan Petroleum Supply Base was the most active issue, climbing HK$4.87.
Meanwhile, Shanghai's A share index edged down 0.78 percent to 1,168.466 points on volume of 839.1 million shares worth 8.8 billion yuan ($1.06 billion), down from 9.7 billion yuan on Wednesday.
Shanghai Bus Industrial Co was the biggest loser on its plan not to make a bonus issue, falling 5.87 percent to 14.85 yuan.
Shenzhen's A share index lost 0.77 percent to 410.94 point on turnover of 8.94 billion yuan, compared with Wednesday's 10.98 billion.
Textile firm Hainan Haide was the poorest performer on the A share market, falling 9.4 percent to 7.04 yuan.
